mainTopic: The עונה (set schedule of marital relations) for different husbands, especially Torah scholars, and stories about the cost to wives when scholars leave home for years to learn.
overview: This amud finishes showing that the משנה's rule about a husband who makes a נדר against relations applies to every husband, even a sailor, because knowing relations are forbidden hurts a wife more than ordinary waiting. אביי rules that a husband may not switch to a job that keeps him away longer without his wife's agreement, since a woman prefers less money with her husband close by. On the sailors' line in the משנה, רב ברונא reports that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר. רב אדא בר אהבה reports instead that the חכמים let Torah students leave for two or three years without permission. רבא warns that rabbis who relied on this paid with their lives, as the story of רב רחומי shows. The גמרא then sets the weekly Friday night עונה for תלמידי חכמים and backs it with a פסוק and the story of יהודה son of רבי חייא. A series of stories follows about scholars who left home for twelve years: רבי's son, רבי חנניה בן חכינאי, and רבי חמא בר ביסא. Each shows the cost to the wife and family. The amud ends as the story of רבי עקיבא and his wife begins, and that story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The vow rule applies to every husband
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer: the משנה's rule about a husband who vows against relations applies to all occupations.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rule applies to all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: This one word finishes an answer that started before this section. The rule about a husband's נדר against relations applies to every type of husband, whatever his job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא had asked which husband the משנה's vow rule (one or two weeks before he must divorce) is talking about. The answer is that it does not depend on his job. It covers everyone, from a man of leisure to a laborer.

keyTerms.meaning: On all of them, meaning the rule applies to every case
The set schedule of marital relations a husband owes his wife

phrases.english: [The tanna taught it] about all of them.
phrases.notes: This finishes an answer from just before here: the vow rule is for every kind of husband, whatever his job.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer begun before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Broadening the scope: the rule is not limited to one occupation.
steps.terutzMaskana: The one-week or two-week vow limit applies to all husbands.

steps.title: But a sailor's schedule is six months
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: how can a one-week vow force divorce for a sailor, whose normal עונה is once in six months?
steps.simpleTranslation: But for a sailor, the משנה says the schedule is six months!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer it just gave. A sailor is normally away for six months, so why should a short vow be such a big deal for him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the vow rule covers everyone, it also covers sailors. A sailor's wife normally waits six months anyway, so a one-week vow does not seem to take anything away from her. It looks strange that this would force him to divorce her.

keyTerms.meaning: Six months, the sailor's interval in the משנה
But look, the opening words of a challenge

phrases.english: But [for sailors] it says six months?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim that the vow rule applies to all husbands.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the vow rule applies to every occupation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sailor already goes six months without relations, so a short vow should not be enough to force a divorce.

steps.title: Bread in the basket
steps.stepSummary: Answer: waiting when something is available is not the same as knowing it is forbidden. A vow makes the wife suffer more.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person who has bread in his basket is not like a person who has no bread in his basket.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a well-known saying. Knowing something is off-limits hurts more than simply waiting for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sailor's wife waits, but she knows relations are allowed whenever he comes home. When a נדר forbids them, she has no 'bread in her basket,' and that makes the waiting much harder. So even a short vow hurts her, and the rule still applies to a sailor.

keyTerms.meaning: Bread in his basket, a picture for knowing something is available to you

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ פַּת בְּסַלּוֹ
phrases.english: One who has bread in his basket is not comparable
to one who has no bread in his basket.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ פַּת בְּסַלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about the sailor.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases by how the wife feels.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A sailor's wife already waits six months, so a short vow costs her nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: A vow makes relations forbidden, and that causes extra suffering. So it still forces a divorce.
steps.whatToRemember: Knowing something is forbidden hurts more than waiting for something that is allowed. That is why a vow is treated strictly even for a sailor.

steps.title: Can a donkey driver become a camel driver?
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב חנן asks אביי whether a husband may switch to a better-paying job that keeps him away longer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב חנן asked אביי: if a donkey driver wants to become a camel driver, what is the rule?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. May a husband change to a job that pays more but means he comes home less often?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives a donkey driver and a camel driver different schedules, and the camel driver comes home less often. The question is whether the husband may lower his wife's עונה on his own by changing jobs.

keyTerms.meaning: Donkey driver, who travels short distances
Camel driver, who travels far and comes home less often

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה בַּר רַב חָנָן לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Hanan said to Abaye:
A donkey driver who becomes a camel driver, what [is the rule]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new practical question about changing jobs.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a husband may change to a job that reduces his wife's עונה without her consent.

steps.title: A woman prefers less money with closeness
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that a woman prefers a little money with her husband near over a lot of money with him far away. So he may not switch without her agreement.
steps.simpleTranslation: He told him: a woman would rather have one kav with closeness than ten kavs with separation.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that the wife's wishes come first. The husband cannot switch to the more distant job without her permission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband might think he is helping her by earning more. אביי says most women would choose a modest income with their husband at home over wealth with him away. So the extra money does not justify cutting her עונה.

keyTerms.meaning: A small measure, here meaning a modest income

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רוֹצָה אִשָּׁה בְּקַב וְתִיפְלוּת
phrases.english: He said to him: A woman prefers a kav with intimacy
over ten kavs with separation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה בר רב חנן's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He may not switch to the more distant job without his wife's consent, because she prefers closeness over wealth.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that a husband may not reduce his wife's עונה on his own, even for more income.

steps.title: The ruling on sailors follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about sailors, and רב ברונא reports in רב's name that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: sailors, once every six months; these are the words of רבי אליעזר. רב ברונא said in the name of רב: the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the משנה about sailors and gives a ruling on it. רב ברונא says we follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה attributes the sailors' six-month schedule to רבי אליעזר, which suggests others may disagree. רב ברונא's report settles that this is the accepted הלכה.

phrases.english: Sailors, once every six months,
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
Rav Berona said that Rav said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַסַּפָּנִים אַחַת לְשִׁשָּׁה חֳדָשִׁים, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה for a new topic: the ruling on sailors.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר that sailors have a six-month עונה.

steps.title: The חכמים let Torah students leave for years
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה quotes רב differently: the חכמים allow Torah students to leave for two or three years without their wives' permission.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said in the name of רב: this is רבי אליעזר's opinion, but the חכמים say Torah students may leave to study Torah for two or three years without permission.
steps.whatsHappening: A second report of what רב said gives the opinion of the חכמים who disagree with רבי אליעזר. Torah students may go away for much longer, even without their wives' agreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's six-month limit is said to be only his own view. The חכמים allow a much longer absence for Torah study, two or three years, and the student does not need his wife's permission.

keyTerms.meaning: But the Sages say, which brings in a disagreeing view
Without permission, here meaning without the wife's consent

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said that Rav said:
This is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer,
but the Sages say:
Students may go out to study Torah
for two or three years without permission.

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, אֲבָל חֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of רב's view, against רב ברונא's report.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, Torah students may leave for two or three years without their wives' permission.
steps.confusionAlert: Both reports are in רב's name, but they are two different versions of what רב said. רב ברונא says the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר. רב אדא בר אהבה says this is only רבי אליעזר's view, and the חכמים allow much more for Torah students.

steps.title: Rabbis relied on this and suffered for it
steps.stepSummary: רבא says rabbis relied on רב אדא בר אהבה's report and acted on it themselves, with tragic results.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the rabbis relied on רב אדא בר אהבה and acted this way themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא comments on how the lenient view worked out in real life. This line sets up the story that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rabbis followed the חכמים's leniency and stayed away from home for long periods. רבא's tone is a warning: doing this cost some of them their lives, as the next story shows.

keyTerms.meaning: They acted on it themselves, and it cost them their lives

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: סָמְכוּ רַבָּנַן אַדְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
phrases.english: Rava said: The Sages relied on Rav Adda bar Ahava
and acted on it themselves [and it cost them their lives].

steps.triggerLanguage: סָמְכוּ רַבָּנַן אַדְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the real-life results of following רב אדא בר אהבה's report.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rabbis who relied on the leniency to leave home for years were punished.

steps.title: רב רחומי misses his yearly trip home
steps.stepSummary: The story begins: רב רחומי studied with רבא in מחוזא and came home once a year on ערב יום כיפור, but one year he got caught up in his learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the story of רב רחומי, who studied with רבא in מחוזא. He usually came home every ערב יום כיפור. One year a topic he was studying held him, and he stayed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story to illustrate רבא's warning. It sets the scene: a dedicated student who came home only once a year, and one year did not come at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב רחומי was doing what the חכמים allowed, staying away for long stretches to learn. This year his learning kept him so busy that he missed even his one yearly visit.

keyTerms.meaning: As in this story about, which introduces an example
ערב יום כיפור, the day before יום כיפור
A Torah topic pulled him in and held his attention

phrases.english: As in the case of Rav Rehumi,
who was often [learning] before Rava in Mehoza,
he was accustomed to come to his home
every eve of Yom Kippur.
One day a halakhic topic drew him in [and he stayed].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the story that illustrates רבא's warning.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that relying on the leniency had deadly results.

steps.title: A wife's tear and the roof's collapse
steps.stepSummary: His wife waited, saying 'now he is coming.' He did not come, she cried, and at that moment the roof collapsed under him and he died.
steps.simpleTranslation: His wife kept waiting: 'Now he is coming, now he is coming.' He did not come. She was hurt, and a tear fell from her eye. He was sitting on a roof; the roof gave way under him and he died.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends tragically. The wife's pain led directly to רב רחומי's death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His wife's hopeful waiting, and then her tear, were taken so seriously in Heaven that he was punished right away, even though he was busy with Torah. This proves רבא's point: being away from one's wife, even for learning, carries serious danger if it causes her pain.

keyTerms.meaning: Waiting and looking out for someone
He died, literally 'his soul came to rest'

phrases.english: His wife was waiting for him:

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא אָתֵי, הַשְׁתָּא אָתֵי. לָא אֲתָא.
phrases.english: Now he is coming, now he is coming. He did not come.
She was distressed, and a tear fell from her eye.
He was sitting on a roof,
the roof collapsed under him and he died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story and completes the proof of רבא's warning.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Causing a wife pain by staying away, even for Torah study, can bring severe punishment. The leniency of the חכמים must be used with great care.
steps.whatToRemember: Long absences for Torah study are allowed by the חכמים, but רבא and the story of רב רחומי warn that a wife's pain is taken extremely seriously.
steps.whyThisMatters: The story balances the lenient ruling on Torah students with a strong warning about how much a husband owes his wife's feelings.

steps.title: When is the marital time for Torah scholars?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when the עונה of תלמידי חכמים takes place.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is the marital time of Torah scholars?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new, simple question: on which night should a Torah scholar fulfill his marital duty? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps were about how long a Torah student may be away from home. Now the גמרא asks about scholars who do come home, and when their regular time with their wives should be.

keyTerms.meaning: The set time for a husband's marital duty to his wife

phrases.english: The marital time of Torah scholars, when is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the story of רב רחומי to a new question about the scholars' עונה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which time is the proper עונה for תלמידי חכמים.

steps.title: שמואל: every Friday night
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל says the scholars' עונה is from Friday night to Friday night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: From ערב שבת to ערב שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question: a Torah scholar's set time is once a week, on Friday night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "From ערב שבת to ערב שבת" means once a week, each Friday night. This gives the scholar's עונה a fixed weekly time, and the next story depends on it.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
From Shabbat eve to Shabbat eve.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת לְעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The עונה of תלמידי חכמים is once a week, on Friday night.

steps.title: The verse 'gives its fruit in its season'
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in תהלים is read as describing someone whose marital time is every Friday night.
steps.simpleTranslation: "That brings forth its fruit in its season": רב יהודה said (some say רב הונא, some say רב נחמן): this is one who has marital relations from ערב שבת to ערב שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק that supports שמואל's answer. The "tree that gives fruit in its season" is a person who keeps his marital time every Friday night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in תהלים describes the righteous Torah learner as a tree planted by water. "Its season" is read as the fixed Friday night time, so the פסוק backs up שמואל's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Gives its fruit in its season

phrases.english: "That brings forth its fruit in its season":

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said, and some say it was Rav Huna,
and some say it was Rav Naḥman:
This is one who has marital relations
from Shabbat eve to Shabbat eve.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק that matches שמואל's Friday night ruling.
steps.raayaObject: The Friday night עונה of Torah scholars
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 1:3, read as referring to marital relations every Friday night

steps.title: יהודה son of רבי חייא and the pillar of fire
steps.stepSummary: יהודה, the son of רבי חייא and son-in-law of רבי ינאי, came home from the study hall every Friday at dusk, and a pillar of fire went before him.
steps.simpleTranslation: יהודה son of רבי חייא, son-in-law of רבי ינאי, would go and sit in the study hall, and every Friday at twilight he would come home. When he came, a pillar of fire was seen in front of him.
steps.whatsHappening: A story begins about a scholar who kept the Friday night עונה faithfully. This step sets the scene for what happens in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows שמואל's rule being kept: יהודה learned all week and came home every Friday at dusk. The pillar of fire shows how holy his coming home was. The pillar also becomes the "sign" that matters in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא, חַתְנֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יַנַּאי,
phrases.english: Yehuda, son of Rabbi Ḥiyya, son-in-law of Rabbi Yannai,
would go and sit in the study hall,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל בֵּי שִׁמְשֵׁי הֲוָה אָתֵי לְבֵיתֵיהּ,
phrases.english: and every twilight he would come to his house,
phrases.notes: He means twilight on Friday, which fits the weekly Friday night time from the steps just before.

phrases.english: and when he would come,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה קָא חָזֵי קַמֵּיהּ עַמּוּדָא דְנוּרָא.
phrases.english: a pillar of fire would be seen before him.

steps.triggerLanguage: יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא חַתְנֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story showing the Friday night עונה being kept.
steps.raayaObject: The Friday night עונה of Torah scholars

steps.title: יהודה stays to learn, and dies
steps.stepSummary: One week יהודה stayed to learn. רבי ינאי did not see the sign and said to turn over his bed, and his words came true: יהודה died.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day a teaching drew him in. When רבי ינאי did not see that sign, he said: Turn over his bed, for if יהודה were alive he would not have missed his time. It was "like an error that comes from a ruler," and he died.
steps.whatsHappening: יהודה got caught up in his learning and did not come home. רבי ינאי was sure he must have died, said so, and his words came true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the story of רב רחומי in steps 9-10: a scholar misses his set time at home, and it ends in death. The פסוק from קהלת shows that a great person's words have power, even when said by mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: The teaching drew him in (he got caught up in learning)
Turn over his bed (a mourning practice)
An error that comes from a ruler

steps.whatToRemember: Two stories in a row (רב רחומי and יהודה son of רבי חייא) show how serious it is for a scholar to miss his set time with his wife.

phrases.english: One day a teaching drew him in.
Since he did not see that sign,
phrases.notes: The sign is the pillar of fire. רבי ינאי is the one who did not see it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי יַנַּאי: כְּפוּ מִטָּתוֹ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai said to them: Turn over his bed,
for if Yehuda were alive
he would not have missed his marital time.
It was "like an error that comes from a ruler,"
and he died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The story's tragic ending.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Missing the scholar's Friday night עונה is treated as very serious; the story ends in death.

steps.title: רבי's son's match with רבי חייא's family fails
steps.stepSummary: רבי arranged a match for his son with a girl from רבי חייא's family, but when they came to write the כתובה, the girl died. רבי asked if there was some flaw in the families.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי arranged for his son to marry into the household of רבי חייא. When they came to write the כתובה, the girl died. רבי said: Heaven forbid, is there some disqualification?
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins about the marriage of רבי's son. When the planned bride dies, רבי worries that something is wrong with one of the families.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי understood the girl's death as a sign from Heaven that the match was blocked. So he asked whether there was a lineage problem (פסול) in one of the families. This sets up the family check in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi arranged a match for his son
with the household of Rabbi Ḥiyya,
when it came time to write the marriage contract,
the girl died.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי: חַס וְשָׁלוֹם פְּסוּלָא אִיכָּא?
phrases.english: Rabbi said: Heaven forbid, is there some disqualification?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אִיעֲסֵק לֵיהּ לִבְרֵיהּ בֵּי רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about marriage among great Torah families.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A broken match led רבי to suspect a lineage problem.

steps.title: Checking the family lines
steps.stepSummary: They checked the family lines and found that רבי came from שפטיה בן אביטל and רבי חייא came from שמעי, דוד's brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sat and looked into the families: רבי came from שפטיה בן אביטל, and רבי חייא came from שמעי, the brother of דוד.
steps.whatsHappening: They answer רבי's worry by checking the family histories. They find two different branches of דוד's family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No family was found to be unfit. Both came from דוד's family, but from different branches: רבי from דוד's son שפטיה, born to his wife אביטל, and רבי חייא from דוד's brother שמעי. The גמרא just records what they found and does not spell out why it mattered.

keyTerms.meaning: They looked into the families' lineage
שפטיה, the son of דוד המלך by his wife אביטל
שמעי, the brother of דוד המלך

phrases.english: They sat and looked into the families:
Rabbi came from Shefatya son of Avital,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא אָתֵי מִשִּׁמְעִי אֲחִי דָוִד.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Ḥiyya came from Shimi, the brother of David.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי's question about a possible flaw.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The families came from different branches of דוד's family: רבי from דוד's son, רבי חייא from דוד's brother.

steps.title: A new match, with twelve years of study
steps.stepSummary: רבי arranged a new match for his son with רבי יוסי בן זימרא's family, and they agreed he would go learn for twelve years.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and arranged a match for his son with the household of רבי יוסי בן זימרא. They agreed with him on twelve years for him to go to the study hall.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי tries again with a different family. The agreement is that the son will first go learn Torah for twelve years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ties back to the theme of Torah students being away from home. Here the plan is a long stretch of learning, twelve years, which the next step will put to the test.

keyTerms.meaning: They agreed with him (set the terms)

phrases.english: He went and arranged a match for his son
with the household of Rabbi Yosei ben Zimra.
They agreed with him on twelve years
for going to the study hall.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲזַל אִיעֲסֵק לֵיהּ לִבְרֵיהּ בֵּי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן זִימְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first match failed, רבי arranges a new one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The new match was agreed on, with twelve years of study planned before the wedding.

steps.title: The groom shortens the time, then marries first
steps.stepSummary: When they brought the bride past him, the son cut the time to six years. The second time, he said he would marry first and then go learn.
steps.simpleTranslation: They passed her before him, and he said: Let it be six years. They passed her before him again, and he said: I will marry her and then go.
steps.whatsHappening: After seeing the bride, the son keeps changing the plan. First he cuts the time to six years, and then he decides to marry right away and learn afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The twelve-year plan from step 18 quickly shrinks. Seeing his bride made the son not want to wait, which sets up his embarrassment before his father.

keyTerms.meaning: They passed her in front of him
I will marry and then go

phrases.aramaic: אַחְלְפוּהָ קַמֵּיהּ, אֲמַר לְהוּ: נִיהְווֹ שֵׁית שְׁנִין.
phrases.english: They passed her before him; he said to them: Let it be six years.
phrases.notes: "Her" is the bride. He saw her and no longer wanted to wait twelve years.

phrases.english: They passed her before him again; he said to them:
I will marry and then go.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַחְלְפוּהָ קַמֵּיהּ אֲמַר לְהוּ נִיהְווֹ שֵׁית שְׁנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The agreed twelve years shrink as the groom sees his bride.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The son decides to marry first and learn afterward.

steps.title: The son is embarrassed; his father reassures him
steps.stepSummary: The son was embarrassed in front of his father, and רבי told him: My son, you have the mindset of your Maker.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was embarrassed before his father. He said to him: My son, you have your Maker's way of thinking.
steps.whatsHappening: The son feels ashamed for changing the plan, but רבי calms him by comparing his choice to the way ה׳ acts. The proof for this comparison comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of scolding his son, רבי says he acted the way his Creator does. Step 21 explains the comparison: ה׳ also moved up His plan to dwell among the people.

keyTerms.meaning: The way of thinking of your Maker

phrases.english: He was embarrassed before his father.
He said to him: My son,
you have the mindset of your Maker —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The father reacts to his son's change of plan.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי approves of his son's choice, comparing it to the way of the Creator.

steps.title: Proof from the פסוקים that ה׳ also moved His plan up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves רבי's comment, 'you have the mindset of your Maker,' from two פסוקים‎. ה׳ first planned a מקדש for after entering ארץ ישראל, but in the end had one built in the desert.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first it is written: 'You bring them and plant them,' and in the end it is written: 'And let them make Me a Sanctuary, that I may dwell among them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where רבי got the idea that changing the plan to 'marry first' copies ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק says the מקדש would come after the people were planted in the land. The second פסוק has them build the משכן right away, in the desert. ה׳ moved His 'dwelling with them' earlier out of love, just as the son moved the wedding earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: Sanctuary, a holy place for ה׳

phrases.english: Initially it is written:
"You bring them and plant them,"
and ultimately it is written:
"And let them make Me a Sanctuary
that I may dwell among them."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי's praise in step 20.
steps.raayaObject: רבי's statement that his son has the mindset of his Maker

steps.title: The son learns twelve years and his wife becomes infertile
steps.stepSummary: After the wedding, רבי's son went to learn for twelve years. By the time he returned, his wife could no longer have children.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and sat twelve years in the study hall. By the time he came back, his wife had become infertile.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on: the son keeps his promise to learn, but there is a painful result at home. This sets up רבי's problem in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son did fulfill the twelve years of learning he had agreed to. The long separation left his wife unable to have children, which creates a real problem for the family.

phrases.english: He went and sat
twelve years in the study hall.
By the time he came back,
his wife had become infertile.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of רבי's son after the wedding.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The son learned twelve years and his wife became infertile.

steps.title: רבי's dilemma: divorce her or take another wife?
steps.stepSummary: רבי asks what to do. Divorcing her would look cruel after she waited so long. Marrying a second wife would make her look like a mistress.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: What should we do? If he divorces her, people will say: This poor woman waited for nothing. If he marries another woman, people will say: This one is his wife and that one is his mistress.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי lays out his problem: both obvious options are bad. This sets up the solution in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son needs children, but each normal solution hurts the wife. Divorce makes her years of waiting worthless. A second wife makes people treat her as less than a real wife.

phrases.english: Rabbi said: What should we do?
If he divorces her,
people will say: This poor woman
waited for nothing.
If he marries another woman,
people will say: This one is his wife, and that one is his mistress.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the wife's infertility from step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to handle the wife's infertility without shaming her.

steps.title: Prayer heals the wife
steps.stepSummary: Instead of either bad option, he prayed for her and she was healed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He prayed for mercy for her and she was healed.
steps.whatsHappening: The dilemma is solved by תפילה, and the wife recovers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither divorce nor a second wife was needed. Prayer solved the problem without hurting the wife who had waited.
steps.whatToRemember: The family protected the wife's dignity and solved the problem through prayer, not divorce.

phrases.english: He prayed for mercy for her
phrases.notes: The text just says "he." It most likely means her husband, though some read it as רבי.

phrases.english: and she was healed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Prayer, which healed her so that neither bad option was needed.

steps.title: רבי חנניה בן חכינאי leaves for twelve years
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנניה בן חכינאי left for yeshiva at the end of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's wedding feast instead of waiting for him. He stayed twelve years, and when he came back the town had changed so much that he could not find his house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנניה בן חכינאי was going to the study hall at the end of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's wedding feast. He said to him: Wait for me until I come with you. He did not wait. He went and sat twelve years in the study hall. By the time he came back, the paths of the town had changed and he did not know how to get home.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about another scholar who left home for twelve years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי asked him to wait so they could go together, but רבי חנניה went right away. After so long, the town had changed and he was a stranger in his own home town.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chananya ben Chakhinai
was going to the study hall
at the end of the wedding feast
of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai.
He said to him: Wait for me
phrases.notes: The speaker is רבי שמעון בן יוחאי.

phrases.english: until I come with you.
He did not wait for him.

phrases.aramaic: אֲזַל יְתֵיב תְּרֵי סְרֵי שְׁנֵי בְּבֵי רַב.
phrases.english: He went and sat twelve years in the study hall.
By the time he came back,
the paths of the town had changed,
and he did not know how to go to his home.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָה בֶּן חֲכִינַאי הֲוָה קָאָזֵיל לְבֵי רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story about a scholar away from home for twelve years.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנניה learned twelve years and came back unable to find his home.

steps.title: He finds his daughter by the river
steps.stepSummary: Sitting by the river, he heard people calling a girl 'daughter of חכינאי.' He realized she was his daughter and followed her home.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and sat on the riverbank. He heard people calling to a certain girl: 'Daughter of חכינאי, daughter of חכינאי, fill your pitcher and come, let's go.' He said: This shows that this girl is ours. He followed her.
steps.whatsHappening: Lost in his own town, רבי חנניה uses a clue he overhears to find his family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He no longer recognized his own daughter after twelve years. Hearing his family name told him she was his, and following her led him home.

phrases.english: He went and sat on the bank of the river.
He heard a certain girl
whom people were calling:
"Daughter of Chakhinai, daughter of Chakhinai,
fill your pitcher and come, let's go."
He said: Learn from this
that this girl is ours.
phrases.notes: He means she is his own daughter, whom he didn't recognize after so many years.

phrases.english: He went after her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how he found his way home after getting lost in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He recognized his daughter by her name and followed her home.

steps.title: His wife sees him and dies from shock
steps.stepSummary: His wife was sifting flour. When she looked up and saw him, her heart fluttered and she died.
steps.simpleTranslation: His wife was sitting and sifting flour. She lifted her eyes and saw him, her heart fluttered, and her spirit left her.
steps.whatsHappening: The story reaches its sad high point: the sudden shock of his return kills his wife. This sets up his prayer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Twelve years of waiting ended in one sudden moment, and the emotion was too much for her. This is the opposite of the reward she deserved, which is exactly what he will cry out about.

keyTerms.meaning: her spirit flew away, she died

phrases.english: His wife was sitting
sifting flour.
She lifted her eyes and saw him,
her heart fluttered, and her spirit flew away.
phrases.notes: "Her spirit flew away" means she died.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה יְתִיבָא דְּבֵיתְהוּ קָא נָהֲלָה קִמְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: He arrives home and his wife dies from the shock.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wife died from the shock of seeing him.

steps.title: His prayer brings her back to life
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנניה cried out to ה׳ that this could not be the reward of this poor woman. He prayed and she came back to life.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said before ה׳: Master of the universe, is this the reward of this poor woman?! He prayed for mercy for her, and she lived.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with prayer reversing the tragedy, just like the first story ended with prayer healing the wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His argument is about fairness: a woman who waited faithfully for twelve years should not be paid back with death. His prayer works and she lives again.
steps.whatToRemember: Both stories end the same way: a wife pays a price for her husband's long years of learning, and prayer repairs it.

phrases.english: He said before Him:
Master of the universe,
this poor woman, is this her reward?!
He prayed for mercy for her
and she lived.
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is the corrected wording. Some versions read it without that letter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the tragedy of step 27.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Prayer revived the wife who had waited faithfully, closing the story.

steps.title: רבי חמא בר ביסא returns home carefully
steps.stepSummary: After twelve years of learning, רבי חמא בר ביסא decides not to surprise his wife the way בן חכינאי did. He sits in the local בית מדרש and sends word home first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא בר ביסא went and learned for twelve years in the בית מדרש. When he came back, he said: I will not do what בן חכינאי did. He went into the בית מדרש and sat there, and sent a message to his house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about another scholar who was away for twelve years. This one learns from the sad story of בן חכינאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last story, רבי חנניה בן חכינאי's wife died from the shock of seeing him suddenly walk in. רבי חמא בר ביסא avoids that danger. He gives his family warning before he comes home.

keyTerms.meaning: the study hall, the בית מדרש
he sent word to his house

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama bar Bisa went

phrases.aramaic: יְתֵיב תְּרֵי סְרֵי שְׁנֵי בְּבֵי מִדְרְשָׁא.
phrases.english: and sat for twelve years in the study hall.
When he came back, he said:
I will not do what ben Chachinai did.
phrases.notes: He's thinking of the story just before this, where the wife died from the shock of her husband's surprise return.

phrases.english: He went in and sat in the study hall,
phrases.notes: The square-bracket letter is the corrected spelling of the word.

phrases.english: and sent word to his house.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חָמָא בַּר בֵּיסָא אֲזַיל יְתֵיב תְּרֵי סְרֵי שְׁנֵי בְּבֵי מִדְרְשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story that directly builds on the lesson of the בן חכינאי story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scholar coming home after a long absence should send word ahead rather than surprise his family.

steps.title: A sharp young scholar impresses him
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא, his son, comes and asks him questions. רבי חמא sees how sharp he is and is saddened, wishing he had raised a son like this.
steps.simpleTranslation: His son רבי אושעיא came and sat before him. He was asking him questions of הלכה. רבי חמא saw that his learning was very sharp. He felt sad and said: If I had been here, I would have had a child like this.
steps.whatsHappening: While he waits in the בית מדרש, a brilliant young man asks him questions. רבי חמא does not realize this is his own son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חמא feels the cost of having been away. He thinks that if he had stayed home and taught a child, he could have raised someone like this. The irony is that the young man really is his son.

phrases.english: His son Rabbi Oshaya came
and sat before him.
He was asking him questions of halacha,
and he saw that his learning was sharp.
He felt sad and said:
If I had been here,
I would have had a child like this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתָא רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא בְּרֵיהּ, יָתֵיב קַמֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story while רבי חמא waits in the בית מדרש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חמא regrets that his absence cost him the chance to raise a great child, not knowing his son already is one.

steps.title: The father stands up for his own son
steps.stepSummary: At home, רבי חמא stands up out of respect for the young scholar. His wife points out that this is his son.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went into his house, and his son went in too. רבי חמא stood up before him. He thought the young man wanted to ask him another question in הלכה. His wife said to him: Is there a father who stands up for his son?
steps.whatsHappening: The young scholar follows רבי חמא home, and רבי חמא stands up for him out of respect. His wife reveals that the young man is their son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Standing up shows that רבי חמא respected the young man as a Torah scholar. His wife's words reveal the surprise. The brilliant student he wished for is his own son.

keyTerms.meaning: he stood up before him, out of respect

phrases.english: He went into his house,
his son went in,
and he stood up before him.
phrases.notes: The father is the one standing up here, out of respect for what he thinks is a visiting scholar.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא סָבַר לְמִשְׁאֲלֵיהּ שְׁמַעְתְּתָא קָא בָעֵי,
phrases.english: He thought the young man wanted to ask him a halacha.
His wife said to him:

phrases.aramaic: מִי אִיכָּא אַבָּא דְּקָאֵים מִקַּמֵּי בְּרָא?
phrases.english: Is there a father who stands up before a son?

steps.triggerLanguage: עָל לְבֵיתֵיהּ, עָל בְּרֵיהּ, קָם קַמֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The story moves to the house, where the son's identity is revealed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sharp scholar רבי חמא admired turns out to be his own son.

steps.title: The threefold cord
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא applies the פסוק 'A threefold cord is not quickly broken' to רבי אושעיא, son of רבי חמא בר ביסא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא applied a פסוק to him: 'A threefold cord is not quickly broken.' This is רבי אושעיא, the son of רבי חמא בר ביסא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the story with a פסוק that רמי בר חמא said about רבי אושעיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cord made of three strands is very strong. The idea is that Torah passed down through generations of one family becomes lasting and strong, and רבי אושעיא is part of that chain.

keyTerms.meaning: he applied a פסוק to him

steps.whatToRemember: Even though רבי חמא was away for years, his son grew into a great scholar. Torah that runs through generations of one family is called a strong 'threefold cord.'

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama read this verse about him:
"A threefold cord is not quickly broken"
This is Rabbi Oshaya,

phrases.aramaic: בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי חָמָא בַּר בֵּיסָא.
phrases.english: the son of Rabbi Chama bar Bisa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A closing comment on the רבי חמא בר ביסא story.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Torah carried through generations of a family, as with רבי אושעיא, is strong like a threefold cord.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's engagement on condition of learning
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא was the shepherd of בן כלבא שבוע. His master's daughter saw his fine character and offered to marry him if he would go learn Torah. He agreed, and she was engaged to him privately and sent him off.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא was the shepherd of בן כלבא שבוע. His daughter saw that he was modest and of fine character. She said to him: If I become engaged to you, will you go to the בית מדרש? He said to her: Yes. She became engaged to him privately and sent him off to learn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new and famous story, about רבי עקיבא and the wife who sent him to learn Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא was a simple shepherd, not yet a scholar. The daughter of a very wealthy man chose him for his character. Her one condition was that he go learn Torah.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva was the shepherd
of ben Kalba Savua.
His daughter saw him,
that he was modest and of fine character.
She said to him: If I become engaged to you,
will you go to the house of study?
He said to her: Yes.
She became engaged to him privately
and sent him off.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא רָעֲיָא דְּבֶן כַּלְבָּא שָׂבוּעַ הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story in the same series about men who leave home for twelve years to learn.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The daughter of בן כלבא שבוע married רבי עקיבא on the condition that he go learn Torah.

steps.title: Her father throws her out
steps.stepSummary: When בן כלבא שבוע heard about the engagement, he sent his daughter out of his house. He also made a vow forbidding her any benefit from his property.
steps.simpleTranslation: Her father heard about it. He sent her out of his house and made a vow forbidding her to benefit from his property.
steps.whatsHappening: The story shows the heavy price the daughter paid for her choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her father was furious and cut her off completely. She left behind great wealth and was left with nothing, all so that רבי עקיבא could learn Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: he sent her out of his house
he made a vow forbidding her any benefit

phrases.english: Her father heard,
and he sent her out of his house
and made a vow forbidding her to benefit from his property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the result of the secret engagement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בן כלבא שבוע cut his daughter off from his house and property.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא returns with twelve thousand students
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא learned for twelve years and came back with twelve thousand students. As he arrived, he overheard an old man talking to his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and learned for twelve years in the house of study. When he came back, he brought twelve thousand students with him. He heard a certain old man saying to his wife: For how long...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא returns as a great teacher. The גמרא is setting up the next scene, where he overhears what his wife is told and how she answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the other scholars in these stories, רבי עקיבא was away for twelve years. He comes back as the leader of thousands of students. The old man's words are cut off here, and the conversation continues in the next part of the גמרא.

phrases.aramaic: אֲזַל יְתֵיב תְּרֵי סְרֵי שְׁנִין בְּבֵי רַב.
phrases.english: He went and sat for twelve years in the house of study.
When he came back,

phrases.aramaic: אַיְיתִי בַּהֲדֵיהּ תְּרֵי סְרֵי אַלְפֵי תַּלְמִידֵי.
phrases.english: he brought twelve thousand students with him.

saying to her: For how long
